It is chosen when faithful estimation of visibility is critical, such as in inverse rendering pipelines where albedo textures must be optimized without shadow artifacts [S2].

The claim states that the technique is chosen when faithful estimation of visibility is critical, specifically in inverse rendering pipelines where albedo textures must be optimized without shadow artifacts. Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Faithful estimation of visibility is critical when the appearance of an object and the illumination are decomposed, e.g. as a postprocessing step of a (neural) 3D reconstruction pipeline.' It further explains that 'Jointly optimizing the light direction and albedo texture... yields significantly more accurate results with Moment Shadow Mapping... while VSM albedo texture shows traces of the shadow because it must account for areas with reduced shadow intensity.' This directly supports the claim that the method is used in such contexts to avoid shadow artifacts in albedo textures.
